newsitem.title: USA: US-China meeting focuses on trade, software - Kantor.
newsitem.headline: US-China meeting focuses on trade, software - Kantor.

text.p: U.S.-China meetings are likely to cover all points of trade friction between the two nations, Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor said Wednesday, but a key focus would be on software.

Two days of meetings were scheduled to open Thursday with Chinese Trade Minister Wu Yi and Kantor announcing details of software contracts between U.S. firms and three Chinese agencies. Kantor said the contracts were a result of a June agreement on intellectual property rights.
The meeting of the U.S.-China Joint Commission on Commerce and Trade also was to discuss establishment of a title verification office in Beijing and additional copyright and trademark training.
"I do not anticipate any dramatic breakthroughs outside of our ability to continue this process," Kantor told reporters.
"Remember, we're building a normal and, hopefully, productive trade relationship which will be reciprocal in nature with China."

While the commission was to focus on 10 business sectors, Kantor said at a private session with Wu, "each of us will raise a number of issues that will cover the waterfront of trade" between the nations. China's desire to join the World Trade Organization -- and U.S. reservations -- was a likely topic, he said.
Kantor said he would raise several market access issues, including rules that virtually cut off U.S. wheat sales. Wu might want to discuss textile exports, he said.
"I would assume we would discuss this and exchange our views," Kantor said of the textile trade.
China is the fifth largest U.S. trade partner and sells far more than it buys. The U.S. trade deficit with China was $33.8 billion in 1995 and totaled $18.5 billion at the end of this July.
